items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And Bert Braud, who was instrumental – classical instrumental – and me. But we spread the chores across.

ctx.x: Did either Branford or Wynton take classes with you or perform in your ensembles?

Yeah, at the school, they were both in the jazz ensemble that I was directing. Also, there was a class that I taught on sight singing and ear training. I developed that at the school. It was a unique situation, because there were only three of us on the faculty. It was a woman – she recently passed – whose primary emphasis was classical vocal. At least one of her students is in the Met[ropolitan Opera] right now. And Bert Braud, who was instrumental – classical instrumental – and me. But we spread the chores…
I know we only have a few minutes. We’ll pick this up if we run out of tape. Your sight singing and ear training: were you able to incorporate jazz?
